title: Rohan's Valtellina cipher letters of 1636 (d'Émery; Savoy and Canisy), Français 5190
correspondents: d'Émery → Rohan, and Rohan's reply; Savoy and Canisy → Rohan
folio_note: Français 5190 reproduction stops at manuscript p. 80
source: BnF harvest; image and print checked 22 Sept 2026
status: Attempted 22 Sept 2026; narrowed 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key split. Savoy and Canisy's 27 May 1636 cipher letters (rohan1636) are printed deciphered in Mémoires et lettres (1758), III, but their manuscript ciphertext and d'Émery's letter of 25 Jan 1636 with Rohan's reply (emery1636, no shared key shown) lie beyond the supplied Français 5190 Gallica scan, which ends at p. 80. The Français 3758 letters of 1635 once in this entry (nos. 100, 104) were deciphered by George Lasry and are louis1635 and chatillon1635.
why: Rohan's Valtellina campaign and the French entry into the Thirty Years' War.
score_note: Reassessed after viewing: the original class A depended on Savoy/Canisy cipher/plaintext pairs, but the paired ciphertext is absent from the linked reproduction. Class C reflects the material now accessible online.
verify: Obtain BnF Français 5190 nos. 171–172 and 214–215; align the Savoy/Canisy ciphertext with the 1758 print.
prior_art: Savoy/Canisy printed deciphered; remaining cipher open (checked 22 Sept 2026)
known: Savoy and Canisy's cipher letters of 27 May 1636 are printed deciphered in Rohan's Mémoires et lettres (1758), vol. III (rohan1636). The 1635 letters of Français 3758 once here (nos. 100, 104) were deciphered by George Lasry (louis1635, chatillon1635).
open: The manuscript ciphertext of Français 5190 nos. 214-215 (Savoy/Canisy) and nos. 171-172 (d'Émery 25 Jan 1636 and Rohan's reply, emery1636) has not been seen: the Gallica scan ends at p. 80; needs BnF images.

title: Antoni Augustyn Deboli → King Stanisław August, cipher despatches from St Petersburg, 1784
correspondents: Antoni Augustyn Deboli (Polish envoy at St Petersburg) → Stanisław August
language: Polish/French (unknown which; the clear despatches of the same days are in Polish)
status: Existing for the despatches the cabinet register covers (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026), not yet matched piece by piece. The King's cabinet kept Deboli's despatches of 1784-85 in clear in AGAD, Archiwum Królestwa Polskiego (zesp. 11) 1/11/0/-/267, 'Deboli' 2 Jan 1784 - 20 Dec 1785 (790 scans). The King's drafts to Deboli for the same years are AKP 268 (419 scans), and AKP 264 has extracts, among them one of 20 Aug 1784. Unprinted: Zielińska & Danilczyk stop at 31 Dec 1782. Systems seen on the ZbPop 10 scans: the old Polish code (ZbPop 444) in 'Sire' despatches, and a second table with 2084, 1103 and 509 frequent (groups to about 3800, e.g. 2 Jul 1784), for which no key of the time was found; ZbPop 451 gives only French fragments on it. Keys of the time: ZbPop 444 'Cyfra polska' of 8 Mar 1783 (1/12/0/-/444, 9 scans) is the old Polish code of 1783-88 (signal group 2345), not the 1789-91 code of targets/deboli1789; ZbPop 451 'Chiffre François Nouveau' of 1780 (1/12/0/-/451, 9 scans) is a French table. Both are online on szukajwarchiwach. We have transcribed both; the transcription will come with a later target. Earlier note: AGAD inventory: "Korespondencja polityczna tajna (pismo cyfrowe) ... Listy zapisane szyfrem"; no decipherment noted. Keys in the same fonds: ZbPop 444 "Cyfra polska posłana do Petersburga Deboliemu" 8 III 1783; 451 "Chiffre François Nouveau envoyé a Monsieur Deboli" 1780; 453-454 the Cabinet's numbered keys 1772-1795 (not seen online). Not on DECODE (list dump searched); not in repo (known.py Deboli, Popiel: no hits). No scan album found on agadd2 for this signature; may be on szukajwarchiwach (blocked).
why: The Polish envoy's secret reports from Catherine II's court to the King; the ciphered parts carry what he would not put in the open despatch.
score_note: Scored from the archive description during the Oct 2026 Polish archives sweep (research/polish_archives/); not viewed
verify: Check the open Polish despatch of the same date (ZbPop 419/420/421/417/415) and any cabinet decipherment; try the 1780 French key (ZbPop 451) and the 1783 Polish key (ZbPop 444) if obtainable; Zielińska's 1780-82 volumes give plaintext for code-group calibration.
prior_art: open as far as checked: Zielińska & Danilczyk print the Deboli correspondence only for 1780, 1781, 1782 (IH PAN, 2015-2017+); later years unedited, Rolnik 2025 says the Great Sejm reports remain in manuscript. A contemporary decipherment may survive in the King's cabinet copies (cf. ZbPop 320, deciphered register for 1774-77) (checked 26 Oct 2026: web search, Zielińska & Danilczyk IH PAN edition series, known.py)

title: Antoni Augustyn Deboli → King Stanisław August, cipher despatches from St Petersburg, 1787: the pieces in tables 9933, 3865, 12282 and the 1789-91 code (the older-code pieces are deciphered in part in targets/deboli1787)

language: Polish/French (unknown which; the clear despatches of the same days are in Polish)
folio_note: 83 pieces, k. 184; also letters of Gołuchowski to one of the King's ministers in the same key
status: Narrowed 6 Nov 2026: the 14 pieces in the older code (key of the time ZbPop 444) are deciphered in part in targets/deboli1787 (deboli1787.html, Brice Dudout, 81.8% of words). Still open: the pieces in tables 9933, 3865 and 12282 and in the 1789-91 code, with no key of the time found. Earlier note: Existing for most despatches (Brice Dudout, 5 Nov 2026). The clear texts of 1787 are in AGAD, Archiwum Królestwa Polskiego (zesp. 11) 1/11/0/-/269, 'Deboli' 3 Jan 1786 - 28 Dec 1787 (661 scans), whose header index runs to 21 Dec 1787. Gaps: 269 has no clear text for 2 Jan or 18 Jan 1787; 25 and 28 Dec 1787 are not in 269 but have the cabinet's decipherments in ZbPop 417 (nos. 002, 003; no. 001 is 21 Dec). Systems, sorted on the opening groups of 56 despatches and 4 Gołuchowski letters in ZbPop 3: old Polish code ZbPop 444 = 22 (with three of the Gołuchowski letters), table 9933 = 19, table 3865 = 14 (two of them annexes), table 12282 = 3 (with the other Gołuchowski letter), the 1789-91 code with leading 4000 = 3, mostly clear = 3.
